To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an approach to generate universal representations for sequences of any length using a large scale dataset with multiple training objectives and our model substantially outperform other representation models on different granularity of text representation.
We propose a novel framework on pre trained contextualized language model BERT, capable of learning universal representations for input sequences with different granularity.

our proposed model is capable of generating fixed-size representations that outperform other state-of-the-art models on sentence level similarity datasets and achieve significant improvements on word and phrase level similarity datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning universal representations of text from pre trained contextualized language model, and the proposed framework has shown great promise in this direction.
the problem of learning universal, fixed size text representation for input sequences of different lengths, i.e., words, phrases and sentences.
the problem that the contextualized representations offered by BERT are not suitable for downstream tasks with input of single sequence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework provides a universal, high quality, fixed length representation for any granularity of text.
our model generates better representations for all granularity of texts, especially on word and phrase level representations.
our model generates better sentence, phrase, and word representations, and the representations can be used to improve the performance in a wide range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to learn universal and effective representations from pre trained language models, and the learned representations are capable of capturing the semantics of input sequences with various lengths.
we are able to generate universal, fixed-size representations for input sequences with any length and the representations can be applied for a variety of NLP tasks.

we are able to generate universal representations for input sequences from pre trained BERT model with multiple training objectives, and our model is capable of generating high quality representations at different granularity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the contextualized language model is not the best model for generating universal, fixed-size representations, but the Siamese Network can learn better representations for sequences of different granularities from large scale of paraphrase and natural language inference data.
, with proper data augmentation, the pre trained language models can be further enhanced for better universal representation learning.
the contextualized language models can be further leveraged to learn more effective representations of text sequences at different levels.
